Whats up SAA

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Once again SAA is in the news - the board is unravelling and now even the pilots have come out publicly against the board and its chair Dudu Myeni

Summary:
WHATS UP SAA

SAA is back in the news once again. Its board seems to be unravelling and its chair Dudu Myeni, friend of the president is according to Business day editor doing just as she pleases.

The Treasury finds its usually solid message wobbling lately, being undone by South African Airways (SAA) and its wayward chair, Dudu Myeni, a friend of the president and, therefore, untouchable

Now the usually cautious pilots themselves have decided to speak out –
On Monday at a meeting attended by 472 of the SAA pilots association the pilots overwhelmingly backed a vote of no confidence in the board of chairwoman Dudu Myeni and her non executive directors. Only two voted against. John Harty chair of the association says:

It is hoped that this vote will serve as a clarion call to Minister Nene and the government that the future of SAA requires immediate and urgent attention and that a new board, fit for purpose and able to deal with the challenges faceing the airline be appointed as soon as possible.




Further information:
WHATS UP SAA

SAA is back in the news once again. Its board seems to be unravelling and its chair Dudu Myeni, friend of the president is according to Business day editor doing just as she pleases.

The Treasury finds its usually solid message wobbling lately, being undone by South African Airways (SAA) and its wayward chair, Dudu Myeni, a friend of the president and, therefore, untouchable

Now the usually cautious pilots themselves have decided to speak out –
On Monday at a meeting attended by 472 of the SAA pilots association the pilots overwhelmingly backed a vote of no confidence in the board of chairwoman Dudu Myeni and her non executive directors. Only two voted against. John Harty chair of the association says:

It is hoped that this vote will serve as a clarion call to Minister Nene and the government that the future of SAA requires immediate and urgent attention and that a new board, fit for purpose and able to deal with the challenges faceing the airline be appointed as soon as possible.

In August Natasha Mazzone of the DA also weighed in. She wrote to the minister of Finance requesting that he appear before Parliament to brief it on whether or not SAA chairperson DUDU MYENI intentions to procure more aircraft in defiance of Treasury advice

Bottom line says Mazzone SAA simply cannot afford to buy more aircraft. But in an editorial today Dudu Myeni writes that “ The SAA strategy has been subjected to intense public scrutiny and debate and that the challenge for SAA and its shareholders has been that this debate is taking place without comprehensive and true information. She bemoans the fact that most of the media reports have focussed on personalities

Myeni argues that SAA needs to grow and defend market share especially in the long haul markets of Asia and the Americas. She says that customers want state of the art aircraft with the latest technologies and world class service.

According to Myeni, SAA has agreed with Airbus to swap delivery of 10 outstanding A320’s for five A330’s which are more suitable for long haul flights. She continues that the cost of five A330’s is about the same as the cost of 10 A320’s. In effect says Miyeni that will mean that SAA can capture more market share and also manage costs better.

That doesn’t sound that unreasonable so what is the problem then?

According to Business Day Editor Songezo Zibi. Dudu Myeni and her board have continued to take decisions that will cost the public billions and the problem he says is that the finance minister, unlike Myeni does not have the presidents ear. She continues to do what she likes regardless of consequence, while the minister has to find creative ways to contain her without firing her says Songezo Zibi.

Another issue seems to be that Myeni is proposing that SAA lease the planes from a South African company instead of directly from Airbus. This has led to severe criticism and will be further interrogated in the story.

Press Release:


SAA In Turmoil
Who will save SAA from its current financial nosedive? The airline already has R14.5-billion in state guarantees, but now they need more money from the taxpayer. In a midnight interdict this week, the courts agreed to gag several publications from reporting on a damning memo that spells out just how dire the airline’s finances really are. This drama unfolds on the back of the pilots’ vote of no confidence in the board, and further resignations from its top management. Now critics are pointing fingers at the chairperson, Dudu Myeni. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


SAA NOSEDIVES FINAL SCRIPT 28th November 2015

Commentary One
SAA is at a tipping point. Its board has been decimated, its finances are in free fall and its pilots have publicly voiced their discontent

Plane touches down

LINK
There has been a revolving door at SAA with a long line of suits either shown the exit or resigning, as one executive put it – he had lost confidence in the board to lead and progress the business

Commentary Two
The board is led by Dudu Myeni,chair of the Jacob Zuma foundation and friend of the president. Insiders say she is running SAA as if she is the CEO.
Former Chief Financial officer Wolf Meyer is the most recent resignation

Derek
Dudu has been referred to as a one person wrecking ball?
Wolf
She is a very strong person and she is in control there

Commentary Three
Last week SAA appeared before a parliamentary subcommittee on finance

Dudu Up Sound
SAA is in the news and there are many issues that are negative about the airline

Commentary Four
SAA has lost over R600 million this year. There have been seven CEO’s in the last 3years. The pilots are in revolt and this week her board gagged the press

Take off SA express

Myeni’s meddling in a multibillion rand Airbus deal could waste millions-
yet she has survived two ministers and is said to be untouchable

David Maynier
Will she do the right thing for South Africa and will she tell us here and now that she will resign

Commentary Five
At the meeting the DA and the EFF turned up the heat

Up Sound Floyd Shivambo
The chairperson is too powerful, the power is because of her links to the president of the Republic. We must speak about this openly

Commentary six
Wolf Meyer was stunned when he discovered that he been blamed in parliament for some of the airlines losses

Derek
How did you feel about the claims made in parliament?
Wolf
I was disturbed, surprised, I was horrified
Derek
Why did you resign?
Wolf
The writing was on the wall there’s a breakdown in trust. I disagree with the direction the board is taking and quite frankly I don’t want to be associated with the decisions and the directions of the board

LINK
Then the pilots came out of their cockpits, and voted overwhelmingly that they have no confidence in the SAA board

Commentary seven
Chairperson of the pilots association, Captain John Harty alleges that Dudu Myeni is pitting the staff against the pilots.

JOHN
She is making out that the pilots are the evil of the airline

Commentary eight
Myeni has said that pilots make up only 12% of the staff but earn 40% of the salary bill

Captain John Harty
When asked what the problems were she said the pilots were draining the airline and when asked to name the 5 most important problems she said number one problem was the pilots. We get singled out and made a scape goat for all the shenanigans and disasters at board level in fact

Derek
But you didn’t take the vote because of retribution around her comments?
John
No it’s a couple of issues we have around corporate governance at SAA

Derek Link
What really ignited the crisis is a deal between SAA and Airbus to swop out the delivery of different planes in a contract that was signed more than a decade ago

Commentary nine
SAA asked Airbus if they could swop 10 narrow bodied A 320 for five wide bodied A 330. Airbus agreed, it would save SAA about R1.6 billion rand and the minister of finance approved the arrangement. SA Flyer editor Guy Leitch has followed the story closely

Guy Leitch
It was an excellent decision – extremely valuable for SAA bottom line and airbus was quite pleased

LINK
So it was all rubber stamped before the changed Airbus contracts were put on the table then Dudu and the board did an about face and refused to sign the execution docs

DEREK
And then Dudu Myeni suddenly comes up with a leasing scheme?
Guy
She wanted to have the leases in rands and she wanted to create a new entity that would somehow buy the aircraft from Airbus and then lease them to SAA in rands

Commentary Ten
Myeni has defended the decision saying it will save money. But the company supposed to buy the planes has been shrouded in mystery.

Guy
I and many others are extremely sceptical that could be done and because so unlikely think there are ulterior motives behind the deal

Commentary Eleven
The minister of finance is now studying Myeni’s new proposal. But the airbus CEO was reportedly furious and has given SAA a thirty day deadline that will soon expire.

Guy
He said just flatly – our rules our ethics committee would never approve the change of the contract to another unknown entity

Commentary twelve
If Airbus decides to invoke the original contract, SAA would suddenly have to cough up 40 million dollars, money Wolf Meyer knows they don’t have

Wolf
I said to the board be aware SAA might face a default situation if we do not approve the transaction and we are obliged to make these payments – unfortunately the board chose not to respond

Commentary Thirteen
Carte Blanche asked Dudu Myeni for an interview but her schedule this week was full and after an initial conversation our calls went unanswered


LINK
This week there were midnight interdicts to try and prevent reports that SAA was in a financial nosedive, but what is ironic is that these reports were based on SAA own internal memo

Commentary Thirteen
SAA has gagged the media from reporting on the memo. With the airline surviving on R14.5 billion in guarantees, and still needing more – the pilots are uneasy.

John
We know that every time we go to the commercial banks we are charged interest and the interest alone is costing us about a billion rand a year

Commentary fourteen
At Satawu’s head office – the only thing they agree on with the pilots is the precarious state of the airlines finances. General Secretary Zenzo Mahlangu laid into the pilots’ vote of no confidence in the board

Derek
Well you see it as a ploy by white pilots to protect their supremacy at the national carrier

Zenzo
We have reasons why we are saying this we have been calling for training of previously disadvantaged they have been blocking this thing. In our view it is protection of their jobs, their privileges and white supremacy

Commentary fifteen
But the pilots say, they don’t do the selections

Derek
Now the union says you are blocking aspiring black pilots.
John
The shortage of black pilots is actually indictment against the country, and the airline and the shareholder. At SAA we have 767 pilots, of that we have 145 pilots of colour, only 67 African pilots male and female. The airline is shrinking, we have 50 pilots less in this company than we did 15 years ago, unless we grow there is no vacancy to take aspiring young black pilots into the company. The airline has stopped the cadet scheme because its too expensive, so all the young black aspirant youngsters out there, there is no way they can get into this career

Commentary sixteen
The union also agrees with Myeni that the pilots are draining the airline

Senzo
Let me tell you why I think there is protection – irrespective of whether the airline makes money – there salaries are guaranteed
Derek
Can I pick you out on that – they say nothing in your response is true
Zenzo
They have guaranteed salaries – we have been talking about this agreement it kills the airline – for more than 7 years now
Derek
They deny its 20%
Zenzo
Its more than that
Derek
More than that!
They deny that completely
Zenzo
I know they are being creative with the truth, it depends on how you calculate your increase.

Commentary Seventeen
And the union says the pilots’ skills are overrated

Zenzo
They are glorified drivers
Derek
Really they are just drivers with all that training and responsibility?
Derek
That does not mean you become a rocket scientist you still remain a driver
Derek
If you reduce their salaries they are going to go to Emirates
Zenzo
May god bless them In Emirates I don’t mind
Derek
You don’t think that is a short- sighted view
Zenzo
No its not

Commentary eighteen
This week the pressure on SAA increased.

John Harty
All we are calling for to the minister is to apply his mind and give us a fit for purpose board who can do the job and at least give us a fighting chance going forward

Derek
Do you feel SAA is a political tool?
Wolf:
I believe so- with direct interference with non- execs dictating how procurement should take place I believe it is being used as a political tool at the moment



Commentary Nineteen
On Thursday the presidency said that government is in the process of
finalising the appointment of a new board of directors as part of efforts of ensure good corporate governance, and that National Treasury continues to work with the leadership at SAA to stabilise the financial situation

THE END 10 03

In at 01 00 00 00
Out at: 01 10 08
Duration 10 05


PROMO ONE 10 seconds
SAA needs more money, its pilots are angry, its board in disarray, and a blocked airbus deal could mean the airline must find millions of dollars it doesn’t have


PROMO TWO 15 seconds
As the turmoil at SAA continues, the union takes on the pilots
Zenzo
They are glorified drivers
Derek
Really they are just drivers with all that training and responsibility?
Derek
That does not mean you become a rocket scientist you still remain a driver


PROMO THREE 15 seconds

Opposition parties have called for the resignation of Dudu Myeni, chair of the SAA board.

DAVID MAYNIER
David Maynier
Will she do the right thing for South Africa and will she tell us here and now that she will resign

metadata.Further information: WHATS UP SAA SAA is back in the news once again. Its board seems to be unravelling and its chair Dudu Myeni, friend of the president is according to Business day editor doing just as she pleases. The Treasury finds its usually solid message wobbling lately, being undone by South African Airways (SAA) and its wayward chair, Dudu Myeni, a friend of the president and, therefore, untouchable Now the usually cautious pilots themselves have decided to speak out – On Monday at a meeting attended by 472 of the SAA pilots association the pilots overwhelmingly backed a vote of no confidence in the board of chairwoman Dudu Myeni and her non executive directors. Only two voted against. John Harty chair of the association says: It is hoped that this vote will serve as a clarion call to Minister Nene and the government that the future of SAA requires immediate and urgent attention and that a new board, fit for purpose and able to deal with the challenges faceing the airline be appointed as soon as possible. In August Natasha Mazzone of the DA also weighed in. She wrote to the minister of Finance requesting that he appear before Parliament to brief it on whether or not SAA chairperson DUDU MYENI intentions to procure more aircraft in defiance of Treasury advice Bottom line says Mazzone SAA simply cannot afford to buy more aircraft. But in an editorial today Dudu Myeni writes that “ The SAA strategy has been subjected to intense public scrutiny and debate and that the challenge for SAA and its shareholders has been that this debate is taking place without comprehensive and true information. She bemoans the fact that most of the media reports have focussed on personalities Myeni argues that SAA needs to grow and defend market share especially in the long haul markets of Asia and the Americas. She says that customers want state of the art aircraft with the latest technologies and world class service. According to Myeni, SAA has agreed with Airbus to swap delivery of 10 outstanding A320’s for five A330’s which are more suitable for long haul flights. She continues that the cost of five A330’s is about the same as the cost of 10 A320’s. In effect says Miyeni that will mean that SAA can capture more market share and also manage costs better. That doesn’t sound that unreasonable so what is the problem then? According to Business Day Editor Songezo Zibi. Dudu Myeni and her board have continued to take decisions that will cost the public billions and the problem he says is that the finance minister, unlike Myeni does not have the presidents ear. She continues to do what she likes regardless of consequence, while the minister has to find creative ways to contain her without firing her says Songezo Zibi. Another issue seems to be that Myeni is proposing that SAA lease the planes from a South African company instead of directly from Airbus. This has led to severe criticism and will be further interrogated in the story.
